focused_whole_view.name: focused_whole_view
focused_whole_view.body_sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.id)
FROM ports AS p
WHERE
  p.admin_state_up = 1
focused_whole_view.description: Task: Calculate the number of distinct ports with admin_state_up = 1 and the number of distinct DOWN ports belonging to security groups where the number of DOWN ports exceeds the average number of DOW
counter_examples: For each of the top 10 tenants with the highest total number of IP allocations on administratively up ports (with at least one IP allocation), list the tenant ID, the total number of such ports, the total number of IP allocations across those ports, whether the tenant has any floating IPs allocated, and the average (across that tenant’s ports) deviation of each port’s IP allocation count from the global average IP allocation count across all such ports. Do not return any rounded answers.

For ports whose status is DOWN, list each port’s ID and tenant ID along with its host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports and the average DOWN-port count across all tenants, plus the port’s MAC address, the running sum of the port’s standard attribute ID within its security group (ordered by standard attribute ID), the security group’s total number of DOWN ports, and that security group’s deviation from the average DOWN-port count across all security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.

For the port with ID `25d421c1-c76d-4c26-9550-9f871a1d5034`, list each allowed address pair’s MAC address and IP address along with the port ID, the bound security group ID, the running average of that port’s standard attribute ID (ordered by allowed address pair IP address, keeping only rows where this running average is greater than 0), and for the same security group also show the geometric mean of standard attribute IDs across its bound ports (considering only ports with standard attribute ID > 0) plus the overall average of these per–security group geometric means across all security groups. Do not return any rounded answers.

For the top 10 tenants with the highest total number of IP allocations on administratively up ports (with at least one IP allocation), and where more than 75% of the tenant’s ports are in DOWN status, return the tenant ID, total number of such administratively up ports, total IP allocations across them, whether the tenant has any floating IPs, plus the number of DOWN ports whose standard attribute ID is above the DOWN-port average for their resource type and the average running sum of standard attribute IDs for those qualifying DOWN ports. Do not return any rounded answers.

For ports bound to security group ID 0008e629-5619-41e0-b86c-4eecfeaacb6c whose standard attribute ID is greater than the average standard attribute ID of other ports in the same network, show each port’s ID, status, allocated IP address, and the running sum of its standard attribute ID within its network; also include (for the matching port status) the port-security rollup label (Enabled/Disabled, including subtotals and grand total rows) and the corresponding count of ports. Do not return any rounded answers.

For ports whose status is DOWN, restricted to tenants that are in the top 10 by total IP allocations on administratively up ports (with at least one IP allocation), list the port ID, tenant ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, and the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row). Also include, for each tenant, the total number of DOWN ports and the average DOWN-port count across all tenants, along with that tenant’s total number of administratively up ports, total IP allocations on those ports, and whether the tenant has any floating IPs allocated. Do not return any rounded answers.

For IPv4 subnets whose DNS nameserver order range is greater than the average order range across all IPv4 subnets, list each subnet name along with its DNS nameserver order range, order variance, coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) of the order values, and the deviation of that coefficient from the average coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) across all IPv4 subnets. Do not return any rounded answers.

For the top 10 tenants ranked by the highest coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) (standard deviation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP) divided by average) of allocated IP address string lengths for ports with port security enabled, list each tenant’s ID, their coefficient of variation (using STDDEV only and never STDDEV_POP), and whether they have any ACTIVE, DOWN, or BUILD ports; and for those same tenants, show details of their DOWN ports including port ID, host, VIF type, allocated IP address, the row number ordered by IP address (using a window frame of 2 preceding rows and 1 following row), the tenant’s total number of DOWN ports, the average DOWN-port count across tenants as a benchmark, and the tenant’s DOWN-port usage category (HIGH_USER/LOW_USER/AVERAGE_USER). Do not return any rounded answers. Classify the tenant as 'HIGH_USER' (at least 50% more than average), 'LOW_USER' (at least 50% less than average), or 'AVERAGE_USER'.

For subnets on networks that have a RBAC action of 'access_as_shared', show each subnet name and gateway IP (including subtotals per subnet name and a grand total) along with the maximum IP version (keeping only rows where this maximum is greater than 3). Also, for any matching IPv4 subnet name, include its dense rank of the associated standard attribute ID ordered by the standard attribute updated-at timestamp (using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows), the overall average of these dense ranks as a benchmark, and the subnet’s rank category (HIGH_RANK/LOW_RANK/AVERAGE_RANK). Do not return any rounded answers. Categorize each subnet as 'HIGH_RANK' (at least 50% above average), 'LOW_RANK' (at least 50% below average), or 'AVERAGE_RANK'.

For IPv4 subnets whose network RBAC action is set to 'access_as_shared', what are the subnet name, CIDR, RBAC target tenant, the running sum of subnet standard attribute IDs within the IP version (ordered by standard attribute ID), the total number of such shared subnets per target tenant and the average of those totals across all target tenants, along with the subnet’s standard attribute resource type and the dense rank of its standard attribute (ordered by the standard attribute updated-at timestamp using a window frame of the current row and the 2 preceding rows)? Do not return any rounded answers.
